_meta.why: The plaque is person-keyed and several people report their year on it is wrong. Years are the stable spine; people are attached to years and can be moved.

role_values.president: Led the student government that year
role_values.regent: Held the student seat on the WKU Board of Regents - a separately elected office from 1968 until the two merged
role_values.unresolved: Shares a year with another name and the split is not yet established

_meta.student_regent_history: The student regent seat was created by state legislation reported in committee in February 1968 and filled in April 1968 by William Menser. It carried no vote for at least four years - students were campaigning for voting power in February 1970 and the Herald was still reporting 'Student Regent May Get Vote' in February 1972. Because it was separately elected, several plaque years carry two names: one president and one regent.

leaders.name: Jim Haynes
leaders.note: First president of the Associated Students of Western Kentucky University, elected 18 May 1966, seven weeks after President Kelly Thompson approved the constitution.

events.title: President Kelly Thompson approves the constitution
events.body: The proposed constitution of the Associated Students of Western Kentucky University was completed in late March and approved on 1 April. The copy held by WKU Archives is dated 7 April 1966.

events.title: Students ratify the constitution, 1,812 to 726
events.body: A four-day referendum. 2,538 students voted - a larger raw turnout than most SGA elections have managed since.

events.title: Jim Haynes elected first president
events.body: Seven weeks from presidential approval to a seated student president. Western Kentucky State College became Western Kentucky University on 16 June, so the university and its student government are almost exactly the same age.

leaders.name: William Menser
leaders.note: ASG president 1967-68. On 4 April 1968 the Herald reported he 'assumes duties as Regent Board Member' - making him WKU's first student regent, two months after the enabling bill was reported in committee. The seat was non-voting at first.

events.title: WKU sends lobbyists to Frankfort for a student on the Board of Regents
events.body: The same Herald issue carries a tuition increase, a discussion group on major issues before the Associated Student Government and a committee investigating women's dormitory rules. This is the origin of the student regent seat.

events.title: A bill to put a student on the Board of Regents reaches committee
events.body: Reported by Ron Lawrence. Western had sent lobbyists to Frankfort for it earlier that month. The same issue carries students berating dorm rules and a letter headed 'Wanted: Work for Judicial Council'.

events.title: William Menser becomes WKU's first student regent
events.body: Two months after the bill was in committee, the Herald reported that Menser 'assumes duties as Regent Board Member'. The seat carried no vote at first. The same issue opens candidate declarations for the next student government election.

events.title: Bill Straeffer wins the presidency; the Herald calls the election a failure
events.body: The issue reporting Straeffer's win also carries an editorial headed 'Elections Illustrate Faults, Indifference'. Turnout anxiety shows up in the second contested election the organisation ever held.

leaders.name: Reed Morgan
leaders.note: Single-year plate. Sits between Menser and Straeffer, whose election the Herald reported on 9 May 1968 - so Morgan likely finished a partial term or held the seat between elections.

leaders.name: Bill Straeffer
leaders.note: Election win reported in the Herald, 9 May 1968, in the same issue as an editorial headed 'Elections Illustrate Faults, Indifference'.

leaders.name: Paul Gerard, III
leaders.note: Two-year plate reading 1968-70, immediately after William Menser took the first student regent seat in April 1968. Almost certainly the second student regent. Early student regents were non-voting 'associate regents', which may explain the longer term. Not yet confirmed.

leaders.name: Paul Gerard, III
leaders.note: Second year of the two-year 1968-70 plate; see 1968-69. The plaque names no president at all for 1969-70 - the only year in the whole record with no president plate. Who actually led the body this year is an open research question for the Herald's spring 1969 election coverage.

events.title: Associated Student Congress endorses the Vietnam Moratorium
events.body: The Herald called it a bold step. The clearest early example of the body taking a position outside the campus fence - the same argument that returns in 2017 and 2023.

events.title: Students start grading the faculty
events.body: An ASG committee compiled the results of Western's first student teacher-evaluation effort. The Herald had already editorialised demanding the tabulation move faster.

events.title: 'Associate' regents want voting power
events.body: Two pieces in one issue: Associated Students seeking voting rights for the student regent, and student and faculty 'associate' regents pressing for a vote. An editorial calls for broad support of Senate Bill 75. Two years in, the seat was still symbolic.

leaders.name: John Lyne
leaders.note: Shares 1970-71 with Larry Zielke.

leaders.name: Larry Zielke
leaders.note: Shares 1970-71 with John Lyne.

events.title: Regents seat eight students on the Academic Council
events.body: An editorial framed it as the Regents opening doors to student expression in academics. Representation was arriving faster in the curriculum committees than on the board itself.

events.title: A resolution on the women's curfew, five months after Kent State
events.body: The Associated Student Congress passed a curfew resolution; the Herald reported abolition was unlikely that year and editorialised that the curfew was obsolete. The letters page in the same issue is almost entirely students arguing about Kent State.

leaders.name: Linda Jones
leaders.note: First woman to hold the office. The Herald of 28 April 1972 carries a piece headed 'Jones, Linda. Reflects on Term' in the same issue as a strike call over dorm visitation.

events.title: Associated Students affiliates with a wider student association
events.body: An early attempt to gain leverage beyond the Hill. Which body it joined is not clear from the article index alone.

events.title: 'Student Regent May Get Vote'
events.body: Four years after the seat was created it was still non-voting. The same issue has the Academic Council clarifying grievance procedure and an Associated Students open session scheduled for 12 February.

events.title: 'Chaos Reigns at Associated Students Meeting'
events.body: The same issue carries students planning a petition to force dorm visitation and a separate piece arguing student interest had collapsed and the Associated Students had followed it down.

events.title: A strike threat over visitation, and six votes won on a university council
events.body: A Mass Action Committee called for a strike over dorm visitation while the Associated Students installed next year's officers. Buried in the same issue: students gained six votes on a university council. Linda Jones reflected on her term.

leaders.name: Edward Jordan, Jr.
leaders.note: Paired on the plaque with Michael Fiorella, who is confirmed as the student regent that year - so Jordan is the president by elimination. Confirm with April 1972 Herald election coverage.

leaders.name: Michael Fiorella
leaders.note: Student regent, not president. Sworn in 26 September 1972 alongside gubernatorial appointees Gerald Edds and Chalmer Embry, who Gov. Wendell Ford had named the previous month.

events.title: Gov. Wendell Ford names two regents
events.body: Gerald Edds and Chalmer Embry. The same issue reports the best ASG course evaluation yet, students questioning the $5 car registration fee, and filing opening for ASG offices.

events.title: Three new regents sworn in, one of them a student
events.body: Michael Fiorella took the student seat alongside Edds and Embry. The same issue reports 'Slack Time at Associated Student Government Congress', an ASG bankruptcy plan and the open-dorm visitation fight continuing.

leaders.name: Steven Yater
leaders.note: No name is listed for 1974-75 as a single term; the next two plates both read 1974-75. Sole name on the plaque for this year and no competing entry, so almost certainly the president. Not yet confirmed against Herald election coverage.

events.title: Gregory McKinney sworn in as WKU's first African American student regent
events.body: Seven years before Julius Price became the first Black gubernatorial appointee to the board in 1981. The student seat integrated the Board of Regents first.

leaders.name: Gregory McKinney
leaders.note: Student regent, not president. Sworn in 19 June 1974 as WKU's first African American student regent.

leaders.name: Jeffrey Consolo
leaders.note: ASG president. The Herald of 1974 reports 'Jeff Consolo Tabs Eight for Congress' - a president making appointments to the Associated Student Congress.

leaders.name: Steve Henry
leaders.note: Check whether this is the Steve Henry who later served as Lieutenant Governor of Kentucky (1995-2003). Do not assert the identification without a source.

leaders.name: Christy Mollozzi
leaders.note: The outgoing president who 'congratulates voters' in the 15 April 1977 Herald is Christy Vogt, and a Christy Vogt letter dated 26 April 1977 sits in the SGA document series. Vogt and Mollozzi are very likely the same person under maiden and married names. Confirm before merging.

events.title: Bob Moore elected ASG president by 26 votes
events.body: One of the narrowest margins in the record. The same issue carries the outgoing president congratulating voters, the faculty asking for a say in hiring, and Western fighting a beer licence for a local pizzeria.

leaders.name: Robert Moore
leaders.note: Elected ASG president by a 26-vote margin, reported 15 April 1977.

leaders.name: Steven Thornton
leaders.note: The April 1979 primary drew 830 voters and put the open-house policy on the ballot.

events.title: 830 students vote in the primary; the Herald runs a defence of not voting
events.body: The Associated Student Government put the open-house policy on the ballot. The same issue carries a piece justifying student apathy in ASG voting - the paper had moved from scolding non-voters to explaining them.

leaders.name: James Hargroave
leaders.note: Surname spelling on the plaque is HARGROAVE. Verify against the Herald before publishing - it may be Hargrove.

events.title: Sandra Norfleet elected student regent
events.body: Reported by Kevin Francke. The same issue has a group set to speak on the Associated Student Government's behalf and Western's 1982 budget coming off hold.

leaders.name: David Payne
leaders.note: One of three names attached to 1982. Likely a mid-year succession.

leaders.name: Sandra Norfleet
leaders.note: Student regent, not president. Election reported in the Herald, 18 February 1982.

leaders.name: Jack Smith
leaders.note: Two-year plate. Either re-elected or the plaque compresses two terms.

leaders.name: Jack Smith
leaders.note: Two-year plate. Either re-elected or the plaque compresses two terms.

events.title: Apathy as an editorial cartoon
events.body: 'Voter Apathy Can be Solved' ran alongside a cartoon on election apathy and a report that a 24-hour open house was under discussion.

leaders.name: Mitchell McKinney
leaders.note: February 1985 Herald ran an apathy editorial and cartoon plus a report on 24-hour open house discussions.

leaders.name: Timothy Todd
leaders.note: Two-year plate. A 1987 Herald piece reports a candidate shortage and mentions a Tim Todd race.

events.title: Twenty years of amendments consolidated into one document
events.body: The constitution of the WKU Associated Students with amendments - the only surviving snapshot of how the 1966 framework had been patched over two decades. A Judicial Council roster for 1986-87 survives alongside it.

leaders.name: Timothy Todd
leaders.note: Two-year plate. A 1987 Herald piece reports a candidate shortage and mentions a Tim Todd race.

events.title: Not enough candidates to fill the ballot
events.body: ASG races faced a candidate shortage; one report notes a candidate entered a race to help a rival rather than to win. The same issue has ASG tabling a phone bill after amendment.

leaders.name: Scott Whitehouse
leaders.note: ASG filed a formal reaction to the General Education Task Force proposal in 1988.

events.title: A formal reaction to the General Education Task Force
events.body: ASG filed a written response to a proposed overhaul of general education requirements - one of the earliest surviving examples of student government intervening in curriculum rather than campus life.

leaders.name: Amos Gott
leaders.note: The best-documented pre-1992 presidency in the archive. Signed correspondence survives on extended library hours, the DUC flagpole, the stadium press box and a local pizza vendor dispute.

events.title: Extended library hours
events.body: Correspondence between President Amos Gott, Howard Bailey, Sally Ann Strickler and Michael Binder. Resolutions went out as letters to named administrators and answers came back.

events.title: The Downing University Center flagpole
events.body: One item in a working inventory of the job that year: the flagpole, the stadium press box, a dispute involving a local pizza vendor and a proposed budget for the Board of Student Body Presidents.

leaders.name: Heather Falmlen
leaders.note: Presided over the vote to rename the Associated Students as the Student Government Association: passed 7 April 1992, ratified by referendum 14 April, effective that autumn.

events.title: Associated Students votes to become the Student Government Association
events.body: The body voted to rename itself on 7 April and students ratified the change in a referendum on 14 April. It took effect that autumn.

leaders.name: Joe Rains
leaders.note: First president to serve under the SGA name.

leaders.name: Donald Smith
leaders.note: Later president of the College Heights Foundation. Interviewed by the Herald in 2022 on what has and has not changed. At least seventeen numbered resolutions survive from autumn 1993 - the fullest single-semester record in the collection.

sources.label: Herald - The making of an SGA president

events.title: At least seventeen numbered resolutions in one semester
events.body: Resolutions 93-4-F through 93-20-F survive in the correspondence files - the fullest single-semester record in the collection, and the best available answer to how much a WKU student senate actually passes in a working term.

leaders.name: Tara (Higdon) Howard
leaders.note: Plaque gives maiden name in parentheses - search both Higdon and Howard.

leaders.name: Keith Coffman
leaders.note: Outgoing letters from this period cover the Dogwood Drive crosswalk and student seating at athletic events.

events.title: A crosswalk on Dogwood Drive
events.body: One of a run of outgoing letters in these years covering student seating at athletic events, ice machines in residence halls, campus safety, professors posting office hours, food court hours, housing scholarships for off-campus students and student health services.

leaders.name: Stephanie Cosby
leaders.note: Letters survive on ice machines in the residence halls, campus safety, food court hours and professors posting office hours.

leaders.name: Leslie Bedo
leaders.note: Appears in the WKU Archives regents index marked as student regent for 2001-02 - useful confirmation that by this point president and student regent were the same person.

leaders.name: John Bradley
leaders.note: Presided over the 2004 Constitutional Convention that created the three-branch structure. Quoted in Herald coverage of the investigation into his successor-elect.

events.title: The Constitutional Convention rebuilds the body
events.body: Three branches - Executive Cabinet, Senate and Judicial Council - drawn from the student body at large. The most consequential clause is the quietest: every enrolled student became a member of SGA with the right to vote in its elections.

events.title: The president-elect is investigated before he takes office
events.body: The Herald reported an investigation into missing funds from an SGA dining account. Articles of impeachment were drafted against the president-elect's existing finance post but the judicial council found the two-week process could not finish before the term ended. Because state law governs the student regent seat, the new constitution required a separate special election to fill it.

leaders.name: Patti Johnson
leaders.note: IMPORTANT: the Herald reported in April 2004 that the president-elect, surnamed Todd, was under investigation over missing SGA dining funds and might resign, triggering a fresh election. Johnson's name on this plate for 2004-05 suggests that is what happened. Confirm before publishing.

leaders.name: Katie Dawson
leaders.note: Named in April 2004 Herald coverage as incoming executive vice president, so she came up through the cabinet.

events.title: The plus/minus grading fight
events.body: An Institutional Research report on plus and minus grading, a protest broadside, a post-winter-term student survey and an SGA handbook all survive - one of the few academic-policy campaigns documented from research through to public agitation.

leaders.name: Robert Watkins
leaders.note: Single-year plate and the only name attached to 2006. No plate covers a full 2006-07 term. Something happened here. Sole name on the plaque for this year and no competing entry, so almost certainly the president. Not yet confirmed against Herald election coverage. Confirmed: Watkins resigned from SGA in fall 2006, partway through the term, which explains the plaque's single-year plate.

leaders.name: Jeanne Johnson
leaders.note: Overlaps the Johnathon Boles 2008 plate. Sole name on the plaque for this year and no competing entry, so almost certainly the president. Not yet confirmed against Herald election coverage.

events.title: Fifty senators write down what a lobbying trip felt like
events.body: After a student rally at the Capitol in Frankfort, dozens of SGA members each filed an individual written reflection, archived one per person. The richest first-person source in the entire collection.

leaders.name: Johnathon Boles
leaders.note: Appears in the WKU Archives regents index marked as student regent for 2008. In office for the February 2008 Frankfort rally, after which roughly fifty senators each filed a written reflection - the richest first-person source in the collection. Sole name on the plaque for this year and no competing entry, so almost certainly the president. Not yet confirmed against Herald election coverage. The Herald's 2013 retrospective records that Boles resigned in January 2009.

leaders.name: Kayla Shelton
leaders.note: Single-year plate; overlaps Kevin Smiley 2009-10. By this period the SGA president automatically held the student regent seat, so a second name in the same year indicates a mid-year succession - a resignation, graduation or removal - not a separately elected regent. Which of the two finished the term is not yet established. An August 2026 open-web sweep found no corroboration of this presidency at all; verify against the digitised Herald before treating the plate as fact.

leaders.name: Kevin Smiley
leaders.note: By this period the SGA president automatically held the student regent seat, so a second name in the same year indicates a mid-year succession - a resignation, graduation or removal - not a separately elected regent. Which of the two finished the term is not yet established.

leaders.name: Keyanna Boka
leaders.note: Appears in the WKU Archives regents index as student regent, 2013. Plaque spells the first name KEYANNA; the archives index reads Boka, Keyana - confirm which is correct.

leaders.name: Janet "Nicki" Seay
leaders.note: Single-year plate immediately before Nicki Taylor 2014-15. By this period the SGA president automatically held the student regent seat, so a second name in the same year indicates a mid-year succession - a resignation, graduation or removal - not a separately elected regent. Which of the two finished the term is not yet established.

leaders.name: Nicki Taylor
leaders.note: By this period the SGA president automatically held the student regent seat, so a second name in the same year indicates a mid-year succession - a resignation, graduation or removal - not a separately elected regent. Which of the two finished the term is not yet established.

events.title: An election result challenged and upheld
events.body: Anonymous accusations alleged Jay Todd Richey had breached election codes on poster placement. The judicial council warned him against future violations and confirmed he had rightfully won.

leaders.name: Jay Todd Richey
leaders.note: Won amid anonymous complaints that he had breached election codes on poster placement. The Judicial Council warned him but confirmed the result stood.

leaders.name: Jay Todd Richey
leaders.note: Re-elected. In office for Resolution 6-17-S, the reparations resolution, which passed 19-10-1 on 18 April 2017 and drew national coverage. Richey publicly framed it as a conversation starter; President Gary Ransdell stated within days that WKU would not adopt it.

sources.label: Bowling Green Daily News, Apr 2017 (archived copy)

events.title: Resolution 6-17-S passes 19-10-1
events.body: Senators Andrea Ambam and Brian Anderson wrote a resolution supporting reparations for Black students, calling for full and free access to WKU for all Black people and asking for a task force on test-optional and geographically weighted admissions. Modelled on a resolution passed at Wisconsin-Madison earlier that year.

events.title: President Ransdell rejects the resolution
events.body: National wire coverage followed, along with a Tucker Carlson interview with Ambam and a wave of fabricated headlines claiming WKU had granted free tuition. Ransdell stated within days that it was not a university position. Both authors described it as a conversation starter.

documents.title: Senate minutes, 18 April 2017
documents.summary: The SGA's own record of the meeting that passed Resolution 6-17-S, the reparations resolution that drew national coverage. Also records Resolutions 4-17-S and 5-17-S and Bill 29-17-S passing the same night.

leaders.name: Andi Dahmer
leaders.note: Took office alongside incoming university president Timothy Caboni, who began 1 July 2017.

leaders.name: Will Harris
leaders.note: From Glasgow. Sworn in as student regent 2 August 2019. His term ran into the March 2020 campus shutdown.

sources.label: WKU News - regents swear in student regent

leaders.name: J. Garrett Edmonds
leaders.note: The COVID year. Almost certainly the most unusual term in the organisation's history and worth a dedicated oral history.

leaders.name: Matthew Wininger
leaders.note: Sworn in as student regent 6 August 2021, at the meeting that renamed Northeast Hall for Margaret Munday, WKU's first African American student to enrol.

events.title: Northeast Hall renamed for Margaret Munday
events.body: Student Regent Matthew Wininger was sworn in at the Board of Regents meeting that renamed Northeast Hall for WKU's first African American student to enrol - the first building on campus named after an African American.

events.title: Cole Bornefeld elected with 49% of 1,448 votes
events.body: Alexis Courtenay took 40% and Olivia Feck 11%. Sam Kurtz and Garrison Reed were elected to the two vice presidencies.

leaders.name: Cole Bornefeld
leaders.note: Elected April 2022 with 49% of 1,448 votes. In February 2023 the Speaker of the Senate brought a censure case against him over anti-transgender posts he had liked on Instagram; the Judicial Council voted unanimously against censure, and a Title IX report seeking his removal was filed two days later. Last name currently on the plaque.

events.title: The Speaker takes the President to the Judicial Council
events.body: Speaker of the Senate Yulia 'Julie' Mishchuk requested a censure hearing against President Cole Bornefeld over anti-transgender posts he had liked on Instagram. Members of the Queer Student Union and both vice presidents attended. The Judicial Council voted unanimously against censure.

events.title: A Title IX report seeks the President's removal
events.body: Filed with Student Conduct. Under the constitution, removing an executive who will not resign requires written endorsement from at least 20% of the Senate, a wait of at least fourteen days and a two-thirds vote of the full Senate sitting as a court.

events.title: Sam Kurtz elected on an unopposed ticket
events.body: With Salvador Leon as administrative vice president and Annalise Finch as executive vice president.

leaders.name: Sam Kurtz
leaders.note: Former administrative vice president. Elected April 2023 on an unopposed ticket with Salvador Leon and Annalise Finch.

events.title: The 23rd Senate corrects its own governing documents
events.body: Three bills from the Legislative Operations Committee: fix references to a 'University Senate' that had since split into separate Faculty and Staff senates, reconcile bylaws language about expelling senators with a constitution that only provides for impeachment, and update committee names that had drifted.

leaders.name: Sam Kurtz
leaders.note: Re-elected unopposed. Warned the Senate repeatedly that an unusually senior chamber meant the 2025 election mattered more than usual.

events.title: A mental health survey, and a warning about the election
events.body: The Senate passed Bill 4-25-S funding a DEI Committee tabling event to gather anonymous mental health survey responses. Dean of Students Martha Sales told the Senate 'you cannot isolate and educate at the same time'. Kurtz warned repeatedly that an unusually senior chamber made the spring election matter more than usual.

events.title: Rush Robinson elected on a turnout of 966
events.body: Elected alongside class, college, transfer, first-generation, Intercultural Student Engagement Center and Honors College senators - constituencies the 1966 constitution had no concept of.

leaders.name: Rush Robinson
leaders.note: Elected 13-15 April 2025 on a turnout of 966. Told the Faculty Senate to 'take a field trip' to see the state of WKU's residence halls. Handed his successor the red suit jacket on 28 April 2026.

events.title: Two tickets take questions in the DSU auditorium
events.body: Caden Lucas with Jakob Barker and Will Derryberry against Jaden Marshall with Kaden Blankenship and Miles VanRude. Chief Justice Sophie Stirling moderated questions submitted by the student body.

events.title: Turnout jumps 66% in a contested race
events.body: 1,601 students voted, 635 more than the year before. Lucas won. The clearest evidence in the whole record that WKU turnout tracks whether there is an actual contest.

events.title: Robinson tells the Faculty Senate to look at the dorms
events.body: Sitting next to Faculty Regent Shane Spiller during a discussion of WKU housing, Robinson told senators to 'take a field trip' and see the state of the residence halls.

events.title: The red suit jacket changes hands
events.body: At the first meeting of the 26th Senate, Robinson handed Lucas the red suit jacket, "the one that Sam (Kurtz) gave me." The same night, Gabby Pace, Cayden Bailey, Maggie Phelps and Jaden Marshall were sworn in to their new roles.

leaders.name: Caden Lucas
leaders.note: From Harned. Beat Jaden Marshall in a contested race on a turnout of 1,601 - up 66% on the previous year. WKU Spiritmaster, chair of the Hilltoppers Vote Coalition, works for the City of Bowling Green's Downtown Development Division. Sworn in 28 April 2026 at the first meeting of the 26th Senate.
